answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a farmer tending an orchard: one tree is cheap, but a thousand fake trees cost a thousand stakes. An identity that misbehaves loses its stake, and its bad reputation follows it like a plume of smoke no new name can hide. Honest agents build an echo of verified transactions over time, so a fresh identity with no history cannot outbid an established one, and the attacker's cost grows faster than the reward.
